texts.preamble: Baby Ashley Abraham -/- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 In The Court Of Harvinder Singh, Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01, (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Award/Judgment Mact Case No.527/2017 Cnr No.-DLWT01-006725-2017 1.
texts.facts: Vide this judgment/award, this Tribunal shall decide claim of compensation on account of injuries sustained by injured Baby Ashley Abraham in a road vehicular accident which took place on 23.10.2015 at about 1:10 AM at Tax Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, PS Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. CASE OF PETITIONER SIDE 2. Succinctly, the case put forward by petition/DAR is that on 23.10.2015 injured Baby Ashley Abraham along with other persons were going on a tour to Manali in a hired Tempo Traveler bearing registration No. DL-1VA-8948 which was being driven by Kamal Garg. At about 1:10 AM, their vehicle reached at Tax Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, P.S. Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. A truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 was parked in the Baby Ashley Abraham -/- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34737690/ 3 middle of the road in rash and negligent manner without any indication or parking lights or reflector in the complete darkness at that place. Due to same, their vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA8948 struck against said vehicle No. HP69A7149. As a consequence, all the occupants of tempo traveler sustained various injuries. Driver/Kamal Garg and Mrs Maya Abraham died due to same. The incident happened solely due to rash and negligent driving/parking of respondent no.01 who has wrongly parked his vehicle in the middle of the road without any indicators/reflectors. Injured was studying in Holy Child Sr. Sec. School, Tagore Garden, New Delhi at the time of incident. The respondent no.01 being driver, the respondent no.02 being owner and respondent no.03 being the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner(s). The applicant(s)/claimant(s) has/have sought Ashley Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors [MACT No.527/2017] Page No.4 of 28 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.07 17:39:21 +0530 compensation of Rs.25,75,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs and Seventy Five Thousand Only) from the respondents. MISCELLANEOUS PROCEEDINGS 3. Notice of the application/petition/DAR was issued to the respondents on which they appeared and filed their WS(s)/reply(ies) to the present petition/application. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.01 &02 4. In gist, the response of the respondent no.01 & 02 as discernible from their reply/written statement is that the respondent no.1 was having a valid driving licence to drive truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 at the time of incident. Vehicle in question was duly insured with the respondent No.3 covering the date of accident. There was no negligence on the part of the respondent no.1. One set of rear tyres of their vehicle has brusted and its excel has also broken down. Respondent no.1 has parked their vehicle to the left side of the road. Respondent no.1 took all safety measures by giving regular hazardous light. He also put some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters can make out that their vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was driving at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle from behind. Incident took place due to the sole negligence of the driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948. With these averments, respondent no. 1 &2 have prayed for dismissal of the same. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.03 5. In gist, the response of the respondent no.03 as discernible from its reply/written statement is that Incident in question took place due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Ashley Abraham Vs. DL-1VA-8948(TEMPO-TRAVELLAR) have not been arrayed as respondents in this matter. Vehicle bearing registration No. HP69A7149 (HGV-Truck) was insured with it vide policy no. 42103/31/15/630002778 for period 03.08.2015 to 02.08.2016 in the name of Sh. Shankar Ram. Baby Ashley Abraham -/- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34737690/ 4 With these main contentions, respondent No.3 prayed for dismissal of the present petition. ISSUES 6.1 After completion of pleadings, the scholarly predecessor of this tribunal framed following issues on 22.02.2018:- 1. Whether the injured Baby Ashley Abraham suffered injuries in the accident that took place on 22.10.2015 at about 01:10 Am at Tax Barrier, near Prem Dhaba, PS Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab due to rash and negligent driving/parking of vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration number HR69A7149 due to wrongful act or negligence of respondent no.1 Ravi Sharma, who was driving the vehicle? OPP. 2. OPP 3. Relief. 6.2 Thereafter, matter was fixed for evidence of petitioner side. PETITIONER SIDE EVIDENCE 7.1 The petitioner's/claimant's father Sh. Abraham K U examined himself as PW1 to establish this claim. He tendered Ashley Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors [MACT No.527/2017] Page No.6 of 28 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.07 17:39:33 +0530 his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A reiterating and supporting the contents of their application/petition. He relied upon discharge summary of Baby Ann Mariya Abraham Ex.PW1/1, copy of Election I Cards Ex.PW1/2 and copy of school fee receipt Ex.PW1/3 in his evidence. PW1 was cross- examined at length by Ld. Counsels for the respondent side which is not reproduced herein for sake of brevity and was discharged. 7.2 No other witness was examined by petitioner side, petitioner side evidence was closed vide order dated 07.03.2022. RESPONDENT SIDE EVIDENCE 8.1 The respondent no.01 examined himself as R1W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors", and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 22.02.2018. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R1W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on his part. He has parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was driving it at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 relied upon the documents i.e. copy of RC Ex.R1W1/1; copy of permit Ex.R1W1/2; copy of his driving license Ex.R1W1/3 and copy of insurance policy Ex.R1W1/4 in his evidence. R1W1 was examined and discharged. Page No.7 of 28 HARVINDER HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.07 17:39:39 +0530 8.2 The respondent no.02 examined himself as R2W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors" and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 22.02.2018. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R2W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on part of respondent no.1. Respondent no.1 parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was driving it at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 was and discharged. 8.3 Respondent no.03 examined ASI Khushal Singh of PS City Ropar, District Ropar, Punjab as R3W1 in connected petition No.476356/2016 in case of Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors as same was ordered to be read in present matter vide order dated 22.02.2018. He in gist, has deposed that he was not the IO of the case arising out of FIR No. 112 in question dated 23.10.2015. He was only assisting the IO in the said case. They received information about the accident from the Civil Hospital, Ropar District Roop Nagar, Punjab at around 12:00 noon on 23.10.2015. He accompanied IO ASI Sarabjeet to the Civil Hospital, Ropar where they recorded the statement of Ms. Reena Raju pertaining to the accident. They reached at the spot of accident at about 4:00 PM after getting conducted the post mortem of two deceased/victims of the incident. They found both Ashley Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors [MACT No.527/2017] Page No.8 of 28 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.07 17:39:44 +0530 vehicles in accidental condition. He saw that two rear tyres of the right side of the truck has brusted. The truck was standing on the right side of the road. The Tempo Traveller was strucked beneath the back side of the truck. IO seized both the vehicles. He identified his statements dated 05.08.2016 and 22.02.2017 as Ex. R3W1/1. He also identified the site plan of the place of accident as Ex.R3W1/2 in his evidence. R3W1 was examined and was discharged. FINAL ARGUMENTS/SUBMISSIONS/CONTENTIONS 9.1 Submissions/contentions of the petitioner side are that the petitioner side has positively proved that the incident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.01. The injured was studying in Holy Child Sr. Sec. School, Tagore Garden, New Delhi at the time of incident. Award may be passed by this Tribunal as per entitlement/claim of applicant(s)/claimant(s). 9.2 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.01 and 02 are that Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was himself driving his vehicle at a very high speed, in a rash manner and negligent manner. The said driver hit their vehicle in question from behind. The petition of the petitioner side may be dismissed. 9.3 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.03 are that the petitioner/claimant has failed to prove that incident took place due to rash and negligent parking of vehicle in question by respondent no.01. The incident happened due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tempo Traveler, therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner(s), hence, Ashley Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors [MACT No.527/2017] Page No.9 of 28 HARVINDER Baby Ashley Abraham -/- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34737690/ +0530 petition be dismissed. It is submitted that at least there is contributory negligence on part of driver of Tempo Traveler.
texts.arguments: Reference in this regard can be made to the prepositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors." reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgments in the case of "Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and Ors." 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and "Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.", 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 etc. 10.2 Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. 11.2 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its division bench decision in matter of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors." (2011) 1 SCC 343 has held : - "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. Baby Ashley Abraham -/- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34737690/ 10 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. In most of the cases, equating Ashley Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors [MACT No.527/2017] Page No.16 of 28 HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.07 17:40:24 +0530 the extent (percentage) of loss of earning capacity to the extent (percentage) of permanent disability will result in award of either too low or too high a compensation. We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for Baby Ashley Abraham -/- vs Ravi Sharma on 5 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34737690/ 12 determination of compensation (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra v. New India Assurance Co.Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). 9. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim.
